headline: Council passes first reading of ordinance 188-26, amending city code chapters 3 and 169, 8-3.
summary: Changes to section 169-47A, on off-street parking lots, were removed from this round because their definitions are not finished. Council gave final approval to a loan order for $11,400,000 for water projects, including the Main Street water main replacement. Council also accepted a committee report recommending acquisition of 98 Maverick Street, which is fully leased for one year from August.
decisions: Approved the Appointments Committee report, including new members for the fire department, cultural council, and conservation commission.
Approved accepting the City Property Committee report recommending acquisition of 98 Maverick Street, unanimously.
Approved removing changes to section 169-47A, on off-street parking lots, from ordinance 188-26 for this round.
Motion to hold all of ordinance 188-26 failed, 8-3.
Approved ordinance 188-26 through first reading as amended, 8-3.
Approved petition 192-26 asking the state for special legislation on digital posting of legal notices, 8-2-0.
Referred orders 193-26 through 196-26 to finance without reading them.
Approved the $11,400,000 borrowing for water projects in final reading, passed by roll call with 11 members voting yes.
Continued the public hearing on proposed poll 19A on Crawford Street to December 1, 2026.
Continued the public hearing on proposed poll number two A on Willmont Street to December 1, 2026.
Motion to enter executive session on Suarez v. City of Fitchburg failed, by unanimous vote.
Approved, by unanimous consent, letting the council president pursue other ways to get the Suarez information.
discussion: Ordinance 188-26 changes: Members raised concerns about senior center parking and fees, and asked for more time to study the changes. The council was told the new fee schedule is not part of the ordinance.

Water loan projects: Council asked about the American Rescue Plan Act funds that will be used with the city's borrowing. The funds were described as already committed, and a figure of about 3.5 million was mentioned for them.

98 Maverick Street purchase: Members asked whether rent would go into the general fund. The answer was that rent would go to the general fund unless the council first approves a revolving fund to keep money for an appraisal before any sale.

Suarez case executive session: No one from the mayoral administration or the legal department attended, so the executive session did not go forward. The council asked the council president to seek the information, and he will try to schedule the session for the next council meeting.
